claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. My son Alex is 17 years old, and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! Before I can assess Alex's eligibility, I need to check the specific rules. Let me read the eligibility criteria first.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on the eligibility rules, I have an important question about Alex:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** This is important because while Child Benefit normally applies to children under 16, it can continue for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training course).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any kind of education or training at the moment. He finished school and hasn't gone on to college or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question:

**Is Alex currently in paid work for 24 hours or more per week?**

This is relevant because according to the rules, you would stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all. He's just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to make a decision about Alex's eligibility.

Based on the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: While Child Benefit normally applies to children under 16, it can continue beyond that age only if the child remains in **approved education or training**. Since Alex is 17 and has left school without pursuing further education or training, he no longer qualifies.

However, there is one option that might help: according to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. If Alex has recently left school, you may still be within this 20-week window. I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to explore this possibility.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

However, you can still qualify for a child aged 16 or over if they stay in approved education or training (up to age 20). The rules state that Child Benefit is only payable for children under 16, or for children 16-19 who remain in approved education or training. As Alex is 17 and not in either category, he is not eligible.
